How to Score This Practice Form

For CTA scoring, use only the 125 items labeled Scored-Style in this document. The 25 Pretest-Style items are included for realistic full-form practice and instructional feedback but are excluded from the recommended scored-style percentage.
Official licensing examinations use procedures that CTA cannot reproduce. A CTA percentage is an educational indicator only and is not a converted official score or a guarantee of passing.
A client discloses escalating partner violence but is not ready to leave. What is the BEST response?
Begin conjoint therapy with the abusive partner.
Tell the client the violence will stop if communication improves.
Order the client to leave immediately.
Validate the disclosure, assess immediate danger and coercive control, support the client’s autonomy, develop a personalized safety plan, and connect resources.
Incorrect. Conjoint treatment may be unsafe in coercive violence.
Incorrect. Violence is not explained or resolved by ordinary communication skill alone.
Incorrect. Leaving can increase danger and must be planned by the client.
Correct. The therapist should combine safety, autonomy, practical planning, and resource linkage without blaming or coercing.
Safety planning is collaborative; avoid both minimizing violence and replacing the client’s decisions.
CTA LMFT WB6; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 3
A client with repeated self-harm, unstable housing, and inability to use an outpatient safety plan requests weekly therapy only. What is the BEST planning response?
Agree to weekly therapy because client preference always determines level of care.
Promise that outpatient therapy will prevent all future self-harm.
Discuss why a higher level of care or additional supports are indicated and coordinate a safer plan while preserving the client’s involvement.
Incorrect. Preference is important but does not eliminate safety-based professional judgment.
Incorrect. Abandonment is not an appropriate response.
Incorrect. No treatment can guarantee prevention.
Correct. The therapist should respect autonomy while clearly addressing why the current level may not safely meet the client’s needs.
When desired care is insufficient, explain the risk, offer the least restrictive effective alternative, and support transition.
CTA LMFT WB6; CTA LMFT WB7; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 4
When is a provisional diagnostic impression MOST appropriate?
Whenever a client disagrees with the therapist.
When the available information strongly suggests a diagnosis but important confirmation, duration, or rule-out information is still pending.
When the therapist wants to avoid documenting uncertainty.
Only when no symptoms are present.
Incorrect. Client disagreement does not determine diagnostic status.
Correct. A provisional label communicates a reasoned working impression while acknowledging incomplete confirmation.
Incorrect. Provisional status is a transparent expression of uncertainty, not a way to hide it.
Incorrect. A diagnosis requires clinically relevant symptoms or conditions.
Choose provisional when the pattern is plausible but material evidence remains incomplete.
CTA LMFT WB5; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 2
A client who recently began using a prescribed stimulant reports sleeping two hours nightly, rapid speech, impulsive spending, and unusual confidence. What should the LMFT do NEXT?
Wait until the next month because increased energy can be positive.
Assume the medication is the sole cause and advise discontinuation.
Assess chronology, prior episodes, substance and medication use, impairment, and immediate risk, and coordinate prompt prescriber evaluation.
Incorrect. Delay may allow escalating impairment or risk.
Incorrect. The cause is not established and medication changes are outside the therapist’s role.
Correct. The presentation requires differential assessment and timely medical coordination because both mood and medication factors are possible.
Incorrect. The immediate problem is not primarily communication skill.
Use chronology and rule-outs; do not choose between mania and a medication effect without adequate assessment.
CTA LMFT WB2; CTA LMFT WB5; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
An anxiety scale score is high, but the client reports that several items were misunderstood because of language differences. What should the LMFT do?
Accept the score as definitive because standardized tools are objective.
Diagnose solely from the total score after translating it informally.
Discard all assessment information from the client.
Treat the score as one data point, clarify the misunderstood items, use appropriate language support, and integrate the result with interview and functional information.
Incorrect. Standardization does not make a misunderstood administration valid.
Incorrect. Informal translation and a single score are insufficient for diagnosis.
Incorrect. The concern affects the measure, not all client information.
Correct. Measures support but do not replace clinical judgment, accessibility, cultural-linguistic fit, and direct assessment.
A test score is evidence, not a verdict; verify administration quality and clinical fit.
CTA LMFT WB4; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
What is a central facilitator task during the initial stage of a therapy group?
Establishing safety, purpose, norms, roles, and realistic expectations for participation.
Ignoring anxiety because it is not therapeutic material.
Allowing one member to set all norms.
Correct. Early structure and safety support cohesion and later therapeutic risk-taking.
Incorrect. Anxiety is expected and can be addressed constructively.
Incorrect. Premature intensity may overwhelm members.
Incorrect. The facilitator remains responsible for the group frame.
Group-stage questions ask what the group needs now, not what may be useful later.
CTA LMFT WB8; CTA LMFT WB11; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A client describes a specific plan to seriously harm a former supervisor and has obtained the supervisor’s work schedule. What should the LMFT do NEXT?
Assess immediacy and capacity, consult as needed, and take legally and clinically required protective actions without delaying for routine treatment.
Ask the client to return next week with more details.
Explore childhood anger for the remainder of the session.
Correct. Specificity, preparation, and an identifiable potential victim create an urgent protection problem.
Incorrect. Delay is inconsistent with the described risk.
Incorrect. Long-term formulation is not the immediate priority.
Specific target, plan, preparation, and access are escalation cues.
CTA LMFT WB6; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 3
Which mental-status domain is MOST directly assessed by asking a client to state the current date, location, and identity?
Incorrect. Insight concerns awareness of one’s condition and need for help.
Incorrect. Affect is the observable expression of emotion.
Incorrect. Impulse control concerns the ability to delay or regulate action.
Correct. Orientation concerns awareness of person, place, time, and situation.
Match the observation or question to the specific MSE domain rather than to the overall diagnosis.
CTA LMFT WB2; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
A client with no psychiatric history develops abrupt confusion, visual hallucinations, and fluctuating alertness after a recent infection. What is the BEST evaluation priority?
Diagnose a primary psychotic disorder from the hallucinations alone.
Arrange prompt medical assessment because the acute fluctuating presentation may indicate a medical condition.
Wait several weeks to determine whether family conflict resolves the symptoms.
Incorrect. Hallucinations alone do not establish a primary psychotic disorder.
Correct. Abrupt onset and fluctuating attention or alertness are red flags for a medical process requiring urgent evaluation.
Incorrect. Psychotherapy is not the first response to a possible acute medical condition.
Acute change plus altered attention or consciousness should move medical assessment ahead of routine formulation.
CTA LMFT WB2; CTA LMFT WB5; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
At the start of a session, a client reports being temporarily located in another state. What should the LMFT do NEXT?
Ask the client not to disclose travel.
Continue because the therapist is licensed in California.
Verify the client’s location, assess immediate needs, determine whether practice is lawful there, and arrange appropriate continuity if routine treatment cannot proceed.
Incorrect. Concealing location does not solve the issue.
Incorrect. The therapist’s location alone does not resolve jurisdiction.
Incorrect. Continuity options should be considered.
Correct. The client’s physical location can affect lawful practice and emergency response.
Telehealth starts with location, lawful authority, privacy, and emergency capacity.
CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 6
A group member repeatedly arrives intoxicated and threatens another participant. What should the facilitator do FIRST?
Ask the group to manage the member.
Wait until the next session to address it.
Stop the unsafe interaction, assess immediate risk and intoxication, and arrange an appropriate level of care before deciding about continued group participation.
Process the threat as ordinary group conflict.
Incorrect. Other members should not bear responsibility for crisis management.
Incorrect. Delay exposes the group to further risk.
Correct. Safety and current impairment take priority over group-process exploration.
Incorrect. An intoxicated threat is not routine process material.
Group treatment does not lower the standard for crisis triage.
CTA LMFT WB6; CTA LMFT WB11; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
An insurer asks the LMFT to exaggerate impairment so additional sessions will be approved. What should the therapist do?
Tell the client to change symptoms in the next session.
Exaggerate because more treatment may help.
Provide accurate, clinically necessary information, decline misrepresentation, and discuss legitimate appeal or alternative-care options.
Refuse all communication with the payer.
Incorrect. Clinical presentation should not be manipulated.
Incorrect. Beneficent intent does not justify fraud or inaccurate records.
Correct. Documentation and billing must remain truthful while the therapist advocates through appropriate channels.
Incorrect. Authorized, relevant communication may be necessary.
Advocacy does not permit distortion; use accurate documentation and legitimate review processes.
CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 6
A client discloses a sexual assault that occurred the previous night and appears disoriented and physically injured. What should the LMFT do FIRST?
Assess immediate medical and safety needs, offer choices about urgent care and advocacy resources, and support the client without pressing for unnecessary detail.
Require a complete chronological account for the record.
Decide whether the client should report to law enforcement.
Tell the client to confront the assailant.
Correct. Immediate care, choice, stabilization, and resource linkage take priority after recent assault.
Incorrect. Detailed recounting may increase distress and is not required for initial support.
Incorrect. The client retains decision-making autonomy unless another legal duty applies.
After recent assault, prioritize medical needs, safety, control, and informed options.
CTA LMFT WB6; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 3
An LMFT discovers an error in a finalized progress note. What is the BEST correction method?
Delete the original note without notation.
Ask the client to edit the record.
Add a dated, transparent correction or addendum that preserves the original record and explains the change.
Incorrect. Backdating misrepresents when the correction occurred.
Incorrect. The therapist remains responsible for clinical documentation.
Correct. A transparent amendment improves accuracy without creating a false history.
Correct records openly; never make the historical record appear different from what actually occurred.
CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 6

A couple seeks treatment for communication problems. During intake, one partner reports recent medication changes, minimal sleep, and impulsive gambling; the other reports feeling unsafe during arguments. What should the LMFT do FIRST?
Pause routine couple assessment to evaluate immediate safety, possible mood or medication factors, and whether conjoint treatment is currently appropriate.
Select a family-systems diagnosis before gathering more information.
Ask the couple to agree not to mention safety concerns.
Begin communication-skills training because that is the stated goal.
Correct. The vignette contains higher-priority safety and medical-differential concerns that may change the treatment setting and unit.
Incorrect. A systemic formulation should follow adequate evaluation.
Incorrect. Suppressing safety information is unsafe and unethical.
Incorrect. The presenting request does not outrank acute risk.
Integrated items often hide a higher-priority task beneath the referral complaint.
CTA LMFT WB2; CTA LMFT WB5; CTA LMFT WB6; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
A family says arguments happen “every night,” but recalls one evening when everyone stayed calm. What should the therapist ask NEXT?
Whether the exception proves treatment is unnecessary.
Which member deserves credit for the exception.
What was different before and during that evening, and how could the family intentionally repeat those conditions?
Incorrect. Failure-focused inquiry may reinforce blame.
Incorrect. One exception shows possibility, not absence of a problem.
Incorrect. Change usually reflects interaction rather than a single hero.
Correct. Exception questions identify existing resources and replicable differences.
Exceptions are useful when translated into specific, repeatable behaviors and conditions.
CTA LMFT WB11; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A client presents with depression and reports a past week of markedly decreased need for sleep, unusually elevated energy, and risky spending. What should the LMFT do?
Ignore the past episode because the client is currently depressed.
Assess the possible elevated-mood episode fully before concluding that the presentation is unipolar depression.
Assume the episode was healthy productivity.
Diagnose attention-deficit disorder from the risky spending.
Incorrect. Current depression does not make past mood episodes irrelevant.
Correct. A history of episodic elevated energy and decreased need for sleep can substantially change the diagnostic impression and treatment coordination.
Incorrect. The associated impairment and change from baseline require assessment.
Incorrect. Risky spending alone does not establish ADHD.
Screen for prior elevated or irritable episodes whenever evaluating depression.
CTA LMFT WB5; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 2
A new client arrives smelling of alcohol, speaks slowly, and has difficulty following questions. What should the LMFT do FIRST?
Complete the diagnostic interview to preserve the appointment.
Interpret the presentation as lack of motivation.
Ask the client to sign all forms before leaving.
Assess immediate safety, level of intoxication, transportation, and need for medical or emergency assistance before continuing routine intake.
Incorrect. Intoxication may make the interview unreliable and unsafe.
Incorrect. The behavior has a plausible substance-related explanation.
Incorrect. A signature does not resolve impaired understanding.
Correct. Current safety and capacity take priority over routine evaluation tasks.
When current impairment is evident, stabilize and assess safety before gathering ordinary history.
CTA LMFT WB2; CTA LMFT WB6; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
A trauma survivor seeks couple therapy because reassurance never feels sufficient. The partner becomes exhausted and withdraws, which intensifies the survivor’s panic. What is the BEST approach?
Stabilize trauma symptoms, map the reassurance-withdrawal cycle, strengthen direct attachment communication, and avoid making the partner solely responsible for regulation.
Avoid couple work until every trauma symptom is gone.
Treat the problem only as irrational thinking.
Ask the partner to provide unlimited reassurance.
Correct. The plan integrates individual trauma regulation and relational responsiveness while changing the maintaining cycle.
Incorrect. Some coordinated couple work may be useful before complete remission if safe and paced.
Incorrect. Cognition alone does not capture attachment and trauma processes.
Incorrect. Unlimited reassurance may reinforce dependence and burnout.
Do not choose between individual trauma and relational treatment when the mechanisms interact.
CTA LMFT WB8; CTA LMFT WB9; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
An adult client becomes emotionally flooded whenever a parent disapproves. Which intervention is MOST Bowen-consistent?
Confront the parent in a joint session without preparation.
Help the client observe family emotional processes, clarify personal principles, and respond with greater thoughtfulness rather than automatic reactivity.
Use rewards to eliminate all emotional response.
Incorrect. Unprepared confrontation may intensify reactivity.
Correct. Differentiation involves maintaining connection while acting from a clearer sense of self.
Incorrect. The goal is regulation and choice, not absence of emotion.
Incorrect. Emotional cutoff is not the same as differentiation.
Differentiate by increasing observation and choice while staying appropriately connected.
CTA LMFT WB11; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A client with recurring suicidal thoughts asks what a written safety plan should contain. Which plan is MOST clinically useful?
Specific warning signs, internal coping steps, supportive contacts, professional resources, and steps to reduce access to lethal means.
A promise that the client will never feel suicidal again.
A requirement that the client contact the therapist before using emergency services.
Incorrect. Vague encouragement is not an actionable plan.
Correct. A useful plan is concrete, personalized, accessible, and linked to escalating levels of support.
Incorrect. No plan can guarantee the absence of future suicidal thoughts.
Incorrect. Emergency services should not be delayed by an exclusive-contact requirement.
Strong safety plans specify what the client will notice and do at each step.
CTA LMFT WB6; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 3

After a wildfire evacuation, a family loses housing. One parent has no access to prescribed medication, a teenager is threatening self-harm, and the younger child is separated from a caregiver. What should the LMFT do FIRST?
Wait until permanent housing is found before intervening.
Triage immediate suicide risk and medical needs, mobilize emergency resources and reunification supports, and then organize short-term family stabilization.
Choose one family member as the identified patient and ignore the others.
Begin processing the family’s grief in depth.
Incorrect. Crisis support is needed before permanent resolution.
Correct. Multiple urgent needs require triage based on lethality, medical stability, and basic safety before longer-term therapy.
Incorrect. Systemic care still requires prioritization across family members.
Incorrect. Deep processing is premature during acute instability.
Integrated crisis questions reward triage: lethal risk, medical danger, basic needs, then stabilization and recovery.
CTA LMFT WB6; CTA LMFT WB10; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 3
A client reports new restlessness and insomnia two days after a medication dose was increased. What is the BEST evaluation response?
Tell the client to stop the medication immediately.
Ignore the change until the next treatment-plan review.
Clarify the timing, severity, prescriber instructions, and safety impact, and coordinate appropriate medical follow-up within the therapist’s role.
Assume the symptoms are psychological because the client is in therapy.
Incorrect. Medication changes should be directed by an authorized prescriber unless an emergency requires immediate medical action.
Incorrect. Delay may miss a clinically significant adverse effect.
Correct. The temporal relationship and possible side effects require assessment and medical coordination without practicing outside scope.
Incorrect. A medical or medication factor should not be dismissed.
When symptoms follow a medication change, assess chronology and urgency before attributing them to the primary clinical problem.
CTA LMFT WB2; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
A couple attends regularly but reports no improvement after six sessions of skills training. What should the LMFT do NEXT?
Review goals and outcome data, reassess the maintaining pattern and treatment fit, and revise the plan collaboratively.
Add several unrelated techniques without changing the formulation.
Correct. Lack of predicted change should trigger reassessment and a coherent revision.
Incorrect. Technique shopping makes the hypothesis less testable.
Incorrect. A resistance label may obscure poor fit or missing factors.
Incorrect. Persistence without evaluation can prolong ineffective care.
When the expected mechanism does not change, revisit the hypothesis before intensifying treatment.
CTA LMFT WB7; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 4
A client concludes, “One disagreement means my partner will leave.” What is the BEST CBT intervention?
Examine the evidence, identify the prediction, develop a more balanced alternative, and test it through behavior.
Tell the client the thought is irrational and wrong.
Correct. Collaborative examination and testing reduce certainty in catastrophic interpretations.
Incorrect. Historical context may matter but does not directly test the cognition.
Incorrect. Argument from the therapist may produce defensiveness rather than learning.
CBT works best when thoughts become testable hypotheses rather than therapist-corrected errors.
CTA LMFT WB9; CTA LMFT WB11; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A client develops panic-like episodes after a recent cardiac procedure and avoids activity for fear of another episode. What should the LMFT do NEXT?
Clarify medical follow-up and symptom timing, assess panic and trauma responses, and coordinate with medical providers before assuming a purely psychological cause.
Diagnose panic disorder solely because fear recurs.
Reassure the client that all symptoms are harmless.
Use exposure immediately without confirming medical guidance.
Correct. The therapist must integrate medical status, trauma meaning, and anxiety mechanisms before selecting treatment.
Incorrect. A diagnosis requires rule-outs and full criteria.
Incorrect. The therapist cannot guarantee that all symptoms are benign.
Incorrect. Activity recommendations may depend on medical status.
When bodily symptoms follow a medical event, combine medical coordination with psychological assessment.
CTA LMFT WB2; CTA LMFT WB5; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
A parent repeatedly asks a 10-year-old to mediate marital conflict. Which intervention is MOST appropriate?
Ask the child to choose which parent is correct.
Treat the pattern as harmless closeness.
Strengthen the parental subsystem and redirect conflict resolution away from the child.
Teach the child more advanced mediation.
Incorrect. Closeness does not justify a burdensome role.
Correct. The child is in an inappropriate cross-generational role, and the adult boundary needs reorganization.
Structural questions often ask which boundary or hierarchy must change.
CTA LMFT WB8; CTA LMFT WB11; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
When a lawful disclosure is permitted or required, what information should the LMFT generally disclose?
The complete record in every case.
Only the information reasonably necessary for the authorized or protective purpose.
Whatever the requester says would be helpful.
Incorrect. The whole record may exceed the need.
Incorrect. Confidentiality has recognized exceptions and authorizations.
Correct. Purpose-limited disclosure protects privacy while meeting the applicable duty.
Incorrect. The requester’s preference does not define the lawful scope.
First identify the authority and purpose, then limit the disclosure to that purpose.
CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 6
A spouse caring for a partner with progressive illness reports exhaustion and resentment. What is the BEST intervention focus?
Tell the caregiver resentment is selfish.
Validate mixed emotions, assess burden and safety, mobilize respite and support, and help the couple renegotiate roles realistically.
Focus only on the ill partner.
Correct. Caregiver stress is relational and practical; support should address emotion, resources, role changes, and sustainability.
Incorrect. Ignoring the caregiver can worsen the whole system.
Incorrect. Separation is not the only or first response.
Caregiver interventions combine validation, resources, boundaries, and realistic role planning.
CTA LMFT WB9; CTA LMFT WB10; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5

A client develops anxiety and insomnia soon after a job loss and does not report a prior pattern of pervasive anxiety. What information is MOST important before deciding between an adjustment-related condition and a primary anxiety disorder?
Whether a family member has ever attended therapy.
The timing, duration, breadth of worry, impairment, and whether symptoms persist beyond the stressor context.
Incorrect. Treatment preference should follow assessment.
Incorrect. Family therapy history is not the key distinction.
Incorrect. Preference can be discussed but does not establish criteria.
Correct. The relationship between symptoms and the identifiable stressor is central to the differential.
Compare onset and symptom pattern with the stressor rather than diagnosing from the presence of anxiety alone.
CTA LMFT WB5; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 2
One autistic partner needs direct language and recovery time after conflict; the other interprets withdrawal as rejection and demands immediate discussion. What is the BEST intervention?
Tell the nonautistic partner to stop having attachment needs.
Require immediate eye contact and emotional discussion.
Create a mutually agreed pause-and-return plan, use explicit communication, validate both needs, and track whether the structure reduces the pursue-withdraw cycle.
Assume autism makes couple therapy ineffective.
Incorrect. Both partners’ needs require recognition.
Incorrect. The demand may increase overload.
Correct. The intervention adapts access while addressing the relational meaning and cycle for both partners.
Incorrect. Neurodiversity does not preclude relational change.
Adapt the process without erasing either partner’s experience.
CTA LMFT WB8; CTA LMFT WB10; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A client has met goals and maintained gains for several months but becomes anxious when termination is discussed. What should the LMFT do NEXT?
Explore the meaning of termination, review progress and relapse-prevention plans, and agree on a paced ending or follow-up arrangement.
Continue therapy indefinitely to avoid discomfort.
Ignore the anxiety because goals were met.
Correct. Termination is a clinical process that includes attachment, consolidation, autonomy, and planning for future needs.
Incorrect. Avoidance can create unnecessary treatment continuation.
Incorrect. Anxiety can be clinically meaningful even when goals are met.
Incorrect. Abrupt ending may disregard the therapeutic relationship.
Meeting goals initiates termination work; it does not eliminate the need to process the ending.
CTA LMFT WB7; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 4

A therapist treating a child in a high-conflict custody case is asked by one parent to write a declaration recommending custody changes. The therapist has not conducted a custody evaluation and has limited information from the other parent. What should the therapist do?

Clarify the treating role, decline an unsupported custody recommendation, provide only appropriate factual treatment information when authorized or required, and refer evaluation questions to a qualified neutral professional.
Adopt the child’s current preference as the custody conclusion.
Write the recommendation because the parent pays for therapy.
Correct. Treating and forensic roles require different methods, data, and neutrality; the therapist should remain within role and competence.
Incorrect. A child’s preference is relevant but not a complete custody evaluation.
Incorrect. Payment does not determine professional opinion.
Incorrect. Role clarification does not automatically require abandoning treatment.
Do not let a treating relationship drift into an unsupported forensic role.
CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 6
Two group members begin criticizing each other, and the rest of the group becomes silent. What should the facilitator do NEXT?
Slow the exchange, clarify safety and norms, help members describe the process and impact, and invite the group back into constructive participation.
Let the conflict continue until one member wins.
Incorrect. Immediate removal is often disproportionate.
Correct. Managed conflict can be therapeutic when the facilitator protects safety and makes the group process explicit.
Incorrect. Avoidance teaches the group that conflict cannot be addressed.
Incorrect. Uncontained conflict may damage cohesion.
Use conflict as process material only after setting limits and restoring safety.
CTA LMFT WB11; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A client has sudden episodes of intense fear after a robbery and also avoids the location, has intrusive memories, and remains hypervigilant. What is the BEST diagnostic approach?
Assess the full trauma-related symptom pattern and chronology rather than diagnosing panic disorder from the episodes alone.
Assume panic attacks always indicate panic disorder.
Ignore the robbery because it occurred in the past.
Diagnose a phobia solely from location avoidance.
Correct. Panic-like episodes can occur within trauma-related disorders, and the broader syndrome is diagnostically important.
Incorrect. The event may organize the entire symptom pattern.
Incorrect. Avoidance is only one feature and requires context.
Do not diagnose from the most dramatic symptom when a larger syndrome may explain it.
CTA LMFT WB5; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 2
A client treated for panic has completed exposure homework consistently, but episodes occur only after episodes of low blood sugar. What should the therapist do NEXT?
Reassess the formulation and coordinate medical evaluation rather than intensifying exposure based on an inaccurate hypothesis.
Conclude the client is secretly avoiding treatment.
Incorrect. The medical pattern is clinically significant.
Incorrect. More of a mismatched intervention may not help.
Correct. Outcome and chronology suggest the original formulation may be incomplete or incorrect.
Incorrect. Adherence argues against a simple avoidance explanation.
Nonresponse plus disconfirming data should change the hypothesis.
CTA LMFT WB5; CTA LMFT WB7; CTA LMFT WB9; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A couple reports “mutual fighting,” and one partner becomes visibly fearful when the other describes what happens at home. What should the LMFT do NEXT?
Assume equal responsibility because both used the word “mutual.”
Teach time-out skills in the joint session immediately.
Ask the more verbal partner to explain the conflict for both.
Arrange separate, behaviorally specific safety assessment before continuing routine conjoint work.
Incorrect. Shared labeling does not establish symmetry.
Incorrect. Joint skill work can be unsafe before violence and coercion are understood.
Incorrect. The more dominant account may obscure risk.
Correct. Fear and possible coercion require private assessment of violence, control, danger, and appropriateness of conjoint treatment.
When fear or coercion appears, assess separately before assuming ordinary couple conflict.
CTA LMFT WB4; CTA LMFT WB6; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
An LMFT must stop practicing unexpectedly because of a serious illness. What should be done?
Activate an emergency continuity plan, arrange secure records and qualified coverage or referrals, notify clients appropriately, and address urgent-risk cases first.
Send all records to a colleague without authorization or lawful basis.
Wait until recovery before notifying anyone.
Correct. Professional responsibility includes continuity planning even when the therapist is suddenly unavailable.
Incorrect. Record transfer must follow privacy and authority requirements.
Incorrect. Delay may leave clients without needed care.
Incorrect. Silence can abandon clients and increase risk.
Unexpected impairment tests whether the practice has a real continuity plan, not merely good intentions.
CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 6
A therapist lacks competence to continue treating a complex eating disorder, and the client fears abandonment. What should the therapist do NEXT?
End treatment immediately after giving a phone number.
Explain the competence concern, arrange qualified specialty care, coordinate a supported transition, and provide appropriate interim continuity.
Continue beyond competence to preserve the alliance.
Incorrect. A bare referral may be insufficient for continuity.
Correct. Competence and continuity require transparent, clinically supported transfer rather than either overreach or abrupt abandonment.
Incorrect. Alliance does not justify unsafe practice.
Incorrect. Honest explanation supports informed participation.
Referral is an intervention when it includes explanation, linkage, coordination, and follow-through.
CTA LMFT WB11; CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A client experiences panic only during heavy cannabis use and for a short period afterward. What diagnostic question should the LMFT prioritize?
Whether panic is common in the client’s neighborhood.
Whether the anxiety is temporally linked to intoxication or withdrawal and occurs independently during sustained nonuse.
Whether the client dislikes the effects.
Whether the client’s partner approves of cannabis.
Incorrect. Community prevalence does not resolve the individual timeline.
Correct. Temporal linkage and persistence outside substance exposure help distinguish a primary disorder from a substance-induced presentation.
Incorrect. Dislike does not determine diagnostic origin.
Incorrect. Partner approval is not a diagnostic criterion.
Ask whether the syndrome exists when the suspected inducing factor is absent.
CTA LMFT WB5; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 2
An LMFT going through a divorce becomes unusually critical of a client who is considering reconciliation. What should the therapist do NEXT?
Ignore the reaction because therapists can compartmentalize.
Tell the client the therapist’s spouse behaved similarly.
Advise separation to prevent the therapist’s discomfort.
Recognize the reaction, seek consultation or personal support, monitor clinical impact, and modify or transfer care if objectivity cannot be maintained.
Incorrect. Unexamined countertransference can affect judgment.
Incorrect. Self-disclosure may center the therapist and reinforce bias.
Incorrect. Advice based on personal conflict is not client-centered.
Correct. Professional use of self requires active management of personal reactions that may distort treatment.
The ethical task is not to have no reactions; it is to recognize and manage them before clients are harmed.
CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 6
During telehealth, an adolescent repeatedly looks offscreen before answering and whispers that a parent is listening nearby. What should the LMFT do NEXT?
Tell the adolescent to confront the parent immediately.
Clarify privacy and safety, determine whether the adolescent can speak freely, and adjust the session setting or plan before sensitive assessment.
Continue asking detailed questions because the camera is on.
Incorrect. Immediate confrontation may increase risk.
Correct. Privacy conditions affect the reliability and safety of disclosure, especially with minors and family conflict.
Incorrect. The situation calls for problem-solving rather than automatic termination.
Incorrect. Visual connection does not ensure privacy.
In telehealth, assess the room, privacy, location, and who can hear before interpreting limited disclosure.
CTA LMFT WB2; CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
During assessment, one parent criticizes the child, the other parent rescues the child, and the first parent then becomes more critical. What should the LMFT document?
Proof that the child is the sole cause of the conflict.
A definitive diagnosis for each family member.
Evidence that the rescuing parent should control treatment.
A recurring interaction sequence and possible coalition that may maintain the presenting problem.
Incorrect. The pattern is relational rather than proof of a single cause.
Incorrect. Observation alone does not establish multiple diagnoses.
Incorrect. A coalition does not confer treatment authority.
Correct. The observed sequence provides systemic information about reciprocity, hierarchy, alliances, and escalation.
Describe who does what next and how the sequence repeats before assigning motives or blame.
CTA LMFT WB4; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
A client has severe symptoms, but medical and substance rule-outs are still pending. What is the BEST planning approach?
Hide the uncertainty from the client.

Tell the client to stop thinking about the deceased.
Incorrect. The guilt belief need not be reinforced.
Correct. Grief work can support meaning, oscillation, and continuing connection without prescribing a uniform process.
Incorrect. Grief does not follow a universal deadline.
Incorrect. Avoidance may complicate rather than resolve grief.
Do not force grief into either constant sorrow or complete detachment.
CTA LMFT WB9; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
Which statement BEST describes informed consent in psychotherapy?
It is a waiver of the therapist’s professional responsibility.
It is completed permanently when the intake form is signed.
It is an ongoing process of understandable information, voluntary participation, and renewed discussion when material conditions change.
It is required only when the client asks questions.
Incorrect. Clients do not assume professional liability by consenting.
Incorrect. Material changes may require renewed discussion.
Correct. Consent is relational and continuing, not merely a one-time document.
Incorrect. The therapist has an affirmative responsibility to provide relevant information.
When choices contrast process with paperwork, choose the answer centered on meaningful decision-making.
CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 6
A client says the therapist’s proposed goal is not important to them. What should the LMFT do?
Keep the goal because the therapist is the expert.
Explore the difference, clarify clinical concerns, and develop a mutually understood goal or document unresolved constraints.
Incorrect. Expertise does not justify unilateral planning.
Incorrect. Disagreement can often be explored and negotiated.
Incorrect. Collaboration does not require abandoning clinical responsibility.
Correct. Collaboration combines client self-determination with transparent professional judgment.
Do not confuse collaboration with either therapist control or therapist silence.
CTA LMFT WB7; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 4
A parent arrives intoxicated to pick up a young child after a family session and insists on driving. What should the LMFT do?
Ask the child to decide whether the parent can drive.
Prevent an unsafe departure if possible, assess the child’s immediate protection needs, arrange a safe caregiver or emergency assistance, and follow any applicable reporting duties.
Document the concern and take no immediate action.
Allow departure because the parent has legal custody.
Incorrect. The child should not carry responsibility for the decision.
Correct. Immediate transportation danger and child safety require active protection and lawful escalation.
Incorrect. Documentation alone does not prevent imminent harm.
Incorrect. Custody does not authorize unsafe driving.
Integrate current danger, child protection, authority, and the least restrictive effective action.
CTA LMFT WB6; CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 3
A long-term client offers a low-cost handmade gift with significant cultural meaning. What is the BEST response?
Accept every gift to avoid cultural offense.
Accept it secretly and omit documentation.
Explore the meaning, clinical impact, cultural context, policy, and potential boundary consequences before deciding whether to accept.
Incorrect. A universal rejection rule may ignore culture and clinical context.
Incorrect. Automatic acceptance also ignores risk.
Incorrect. Secrecy undermines transparency and reflection.
Correct. Ethical boundary decisions are contextual and should consider value, meaning, timing, exploitation risk, and treatment impact.
Avoid rigid gift rules; analyze meaning, value, timing, power, and foreseeable impact.
CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 6

A client reports unwanted intrusive thoughts of harming a loved one, finds them distressing, and engages in rituals to prevent harm. Which feature MOST supports an obsessive-compulsive formulation rather than a psychotic one?
The thoughts are experienced as unwanted and inconsistent with the client’s values, with preserved awareness that rituals are excessive or uncertain.
Correct. Ego-dystonic intrusive thoughts and some insight are more consistent with obsessions than fixed delusional belief.
Incorrect. Repetition alone does not distinguish the disorders.
Incorrect. Harm content can occur in several conditions.
Focus on the client’s relationship to the thought—belief, certainty, meaning, and insight—not only its content.
CTA LMFT WB5; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 2
A family’s adolescent conflict escalates when parents disagree in front of the child, and the child then threatens school refusal. Which plan is BEST?
Address school-safety and attendance needs, strengthen coordinated parental responses, reduce triangulation, and track both conflict sequences and school participation.
Use a vague goal of improving family functioning.
Ask parents to alternate taking the child’s side.
Correct. The plan targets the maintaining family sequence and includes concrete functional outcomes.
Incorrect. A vague goal cannot guide or measure treatment.
Incorrect. Individual motivation alone does not address the parental pattern.
Incorrect. Alternating alliances would preserve triangulation.
Integrated planning links systemic mechanism, immediate function, and observable outcomes.
CTA LMFT WB7; CTA LMFT WB8; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 4
A client is not ready to stop drinking but wants fewer relationship and health consequences. What is the BEST response?
Refuse treatment until complete abstinence is chosen.
Collaboratively identify achievable risk-reduction goals while continuing to assess severity, safety, and readiness for additional change.
Ignore drinking and focus only on the partner.
Assure the client that reduced use is always safe.
Incorrect. An abstinence-only entry requirement may reduce engagement when not clinically required.
Correct. Harm reduction can engage the client and reduce risk without abandoning assessment or future change.
Incorrect. Substance use remains relevant to relational functioning and safety.
Incorrect. No level of use can be declared universally safe for every client.
Meet the client at the current stage while keeping risk and broader options visible.
CTA LMFT WB9; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A child’s school, divorced parents, and pediatrician each request different treatment priorities. What should the LMFT do FIRST?
Follow whichever parent contacts the therapist most often.
Clarify authority, roles, releases, and the child’s clinical needs, then establish a coordinated hierarchy of goals with the appropriate decision-makers.
Follow the school because it sees the child daily.
Combine every request into one large goal list.
Incorrect. Persistence does not determine the treatment plan.
Correct. Planning must distinguish legal and clinical authority, relevance, and priority before combining third-party requests.
Incorrect. Frequency of contact does not establish authority.
Incorrect. An unprioritized list may be contradictory and unmanageable.
When multiple systems compete, clarify who can decide, who can inform, and what the assessment supports.
CTA LMFT WB7; CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 4
A client’s symptom score improves, but work attendance and relationship functioning do not. What should the LMFT conclude?
Treatment is complete because the score improved.
Progress is partial, and the plan should be reviewed using both symptom and functional outcomes.
Incorrect. Nonresponse in some areas does not prove resistance.
Incorrect. A single indicator does not establish full recovery.
Correct. Outcome evaluation should integrate symptoms, functioning, goals, and the client’s experience.
Incorrect. The measure may be informative but incomplete.
Use multiple indicators and ask whether the change matters in daily life.
CTA LMFT WB7; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 4
A client becomes visibly tense when asked for detailed trauma information during the first session. What should the LMFT do?
Interpret tension as evidence that the event did not occur.
Require a complete trauma narrative before continuing.
Change the subject permanently and never revisit trauma.
Acknowledge the reaction, assess immediate safety and current symptoms, obtain only the information necessary for present care, and pace further exploration collaboratively.
Incorrect. Tension does not determine factual accuracy.
Incorrect. Forced detail can increase distress and is usually unnecessary at intake.
Incorrect. Avoidance may leave important needs unassessed.
Correct. Trauma-informed assessment balances necessary safety and diagnostic information with choice, pacing, and stabilization.
Ask what is needed now; do not confuse comprehensive eventual understanding with immediate detailed disclosure.
CTA LMFT WB4; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
An autistic adult finds unstructured emotional discussion overwhelming. Which adaptation is MOST appropriate?
Require eye contact as proof of engagement.
Use clear agendas, concrete language, predictable pacing, and collaborative sensory or communication accommodations.
Conclude the client lacks emotional capacity.
Incorrect. Unnecessary ambiguity may reduce access.
Incorrect. Eye contact is not a universal measure of engagement.
Correct. Structure and accessibility can improve participation without pathologizing neurodivergent communication.
Incorrect. Communication style does not equal absence of emotion.
Competent adaptation changes format and access while preserving the therapeutic goal.
CTA LMFT WB10; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
What is the main purpose of differential diagnosis?
To compare plausible explanations and determine which best accounts for the symptoms, chronology, impairment, and rule-outs.
To list every diagnosis the client has ever heard of.
To identify the most severe-sounding label.
To replace clinical assessment with a checklist.
Correct. Differential reasoning evaluates competing hypotheses rather than jumping to the first familiar label.
Incorrect. An indiscriminate list does not clarify the best explanation.
Incorrect. Severity of a label is not the criterion.
Incorrect. Criteria support but do not replace clinical judgment and context.
Ask what else could explain the presentation and what evidence would distinguish the possibilities.
CTA LMFT WB5; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 2
A parent and child are beginning contact after a long separation. The parent wants an immediate overnight visit, but the child shows fear and minimal trust. What should the therapist do?
Use gradual, developmentally paced contact, assess safety and the child’s responses, and increase intensity only as evidence supports readiness.
Require the overnight visit to prove commitment.
Allow the parent to set the pace alone.
Avoid all future contact because the child is anxious.
Correct. Reunification should be paced by safety, attachment, developmental needs, and observed response.
Incorrect. Forced intensity may worsen fear and attachment disruption.
Incorrect. Adult preference is not the only consideration.
Incorrect. Anxiety calls for careful pacing rather than permanent avoidance.
Increase relational demand only after the system demonstrates capacity for the current step.
CTA LMFT WB8; CTA LMFT WB10; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A client says a prior therapist interpreted strong family involvement as unhealthy dependence. What is the BEST response during evaluation?
Avoid asking about culture because it could be uncomfortable.
Assure the client that all family involvement is healthy.
Explore the client’s cultural and personal meaning of family involvement before deciding whether it supports or interferes with functioning.
Assume the prior therapist was correct because independence is always the goal.
Incorrect. Avoidance prevents accurate and respectful assessment.
Incorrect. Family involvement can be supportive or constraining depending on context.
Correct. Cultural humility requires curiosity about meaning, function, power, and context rather than imposing a universal norm.
Incorrect. Independence is not the only legitimate relational value.
Assess function and meaning before labeling a culturally shaped pattern as pathological.
CTA LMFT WB3; CTA LMFT WB10; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
A client with bipolar disorder, diabetes, and family conflict is missing medication and medical appointments because relatives give contradictory advice. What should the LMFT do?
Choose which medical advice is correct.
With authorization, coordinate a clear care plan across providers, clarify family roles, address barriers and beliefs, and support the client’s decision-making and follow-through.
Tell the family to manage all medications.
Focus only on family communication without provider coordination.
Incorrect. Medical decisions belong with qualified providers.
Correct. The therapist can improve coordination and family process without practicing medicine or removing autonomy.
Incorrect. Family support should not replace the client or prescriber.
Incorrect. Fragmented care is part of the maintaining problem.
Interdisciplinary treatment asks who owns each decision and how information and follow-up will flow.
CTA LMFT WB9; CTA LMFT WB11; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
An 8-year-old becomes clingy and has sleep difficulty after the family moves and a new sibling is born. What should the LMFT evaluate FIRST?
Whether the child is intentionally manipulating the parents.
The timing, duration, developmental fit, family transition, impairment, and whether symptoms are improving or worsening.
Incorrect. School data are useful but too narrow.
Incorrect. Intent should not be assumed from distress behavior.
Incorrect. Personality diagnosis is not supported by the information.
Correct. The presentation may reflect a developmental response to multiple transitions, but severity and impairment still require assessment.
With children, compare behavior with developmental expectations and recent transitions before making a fixed interpretation.
CTA LMFT WB3; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 1
A newly formed stepfamily expects immediate closeness, and the stepparent becomes punitive when the child remains distant. What should the therapist do NEXT?
Require the child to call the stepparent “Mom” or “Dad.”
Interpret distance as rejection of the marriage.
Normalize gradual relationship development, clarify realistic roles, support the biological parent’s leadership, and create low-pressure opportunities for connection.
Give the stepparent full disciplinary authority immediately.
Incorrect. Forced labels may intensify resistance.
Incorrect. Distance can reflect transition rather than deliberate rejection.
Correct. Stepfamily integration usually requires time, role clarity, and developmentally appropriate expectations.
Incorrect. Premature authority can worsen loyalty conflicts.
In stepfamilies, pace closeness and authority rather than copying first-family expectations.
CTA LMFT WB8; CTA LMFT WB10; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A court-referred client says, “I am only here because I have to be, and I do not need to change.” What should the therapist do NEXT?
Clarify the mandate and available choices, explore the client’s own concerns, and look for personally meaningful discrepancies without arguing.
End the session because motivation is absent.
Incorrect. Ignoring the mandate undermines informed consent.
Incorrect. Threats increase coercion and resistance.
Correct. MI can be used in mandated contexts by being transparent and evoking the client’s own goals and choices.
Incorrect. Low readiness is a treatment focus, not automatic grounds for ending.
Mandate limits choice about attendance, not every choice within treatment.
CTA LMFT WB9; CTA LMFT WB12; Pearson VUE LMFT Outline Area 5
A therapist conceptualizes a couple’s distress as a pursue-withdraw attachment cycle. Which plan is MOST coherent?
Ask the couple to avoid emotional topics permanently.
Use only behavioral contracts without discussing attachment cues.
Increase emotional accessibility and responsiveness while helping partners identify and reorganize the cycle.
Incorrect. Avoidance would maintain the pattern.
Incorrect. Historical information may inform the case but is not the sole treatment target.
Incorrect. Behavioral tools may help but do not directly address the stated cycle when used alone.
Correct. The intervention targets the mechanism named in the formulation.
Match the intervention to the maintaining mechanism, not merely to the therapist’s preferred technique.
